articles.title: The X-Men Became Marvel Legends by Borrowing a Winning Formula From DC, Just Not the One You Think

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The X-Men are basically the once and future king of Marvel. The team is finally about to make its full MCU debut after years of teases, first appearing as a team in Avengers: Doomsday (and perhaps Avengers: Secret Wars , but most fans assume the FoX-Men are about to die in the earlier movie) before an all-new cast of mutants takes their place on the big screen in 2028. Marvel now has the power of Disney behind them; the X-Men are going to be everywhere in the years to come. The MCU has fallen from grace, but I think we all know just how massive the men and women of X are going to be in the years to come.

This isn't the first time that the X-Men are positioned to become the most popular team in comics. The team was the biggest superhero team of the '80s and '90s, with the rise of the Avengers in the '00s finally seeing the X-Men take a back seat to another team. Books like Uncanny X-Men , X-Men , and Wolverine sold in the six figure range for years, with Uncanny and X-Men holding the top spots of the sales charts for nearly every month of the '80s and '90s. Their rise in the mid '70s came during a Marvel boom period, where the House of Ideas was proving that that successes of the Silver Age weren't a fluke. Those issues of X-Men went in a new direction with their new team, with the X-Men becoming the greatest superhero soap opera of all time. However, they weren't the first superhero soap opera; that was the Legion of Superheroes . The X-Men stole the Legion approach and that's the only reason they've reached the level of popularity they have.

So, to begin with, we need to define what I mean when I say "superhero soap opera". Basically, this approach to superheroes is all about how much the stories revolve around the personal lives of the characters. All superhero books get into that sort of thing, but the true superhero soap opera books are all about it. You have a bunch of beautiful, damaged people together; the shenanigans of their life are going to be entertaining.

The Legion of Superheroes were one of the first practitioners of this art. The Legion has a massive membership , the team consisting of alien teens from across the 31st century. Half of the fun of the Legion is the web of relationships and the way they all react to each other. There are cliques within the team and the various members all have their own supporting characters and enemies. While Legion comics gave readers pulse-pounding superhero action, it also gave readers the kind of soap opera stories that hooked them.

The Legion are integral to the history of DC , but in recent years have fallen from grace, their stories much too complicated. One of the things about jumping into the various Legion reboots is that all of them play off of one another. Knowing the relationships and the team members' histories makes it easier to get into them. They are the most daunting team to get into in comics. Sure, the superhero soap opera basics are always fun, but without knowing the history, it doesn't always hit the same.

The Silver Age X-Men were a lot like the Legion; they were both teen teams, for example. However, the difference is the X-Men's civil rights connections, something that was played up in the early months of their adventures, as they battled both evil mutants and human bigots. However, the team never really caught on. Fans just didn't really care about them as characters, which was rare for Marvel in the Silver Age. By contrast, the Legion focused on its characters and their lives and fans loved it. The X-Men had cool villains, great costumes, and entertaining powers, but they didn't have good characters, which led to them almost going the way of the dodo.

Giant-Size X-Men #1 is where the major Legion similarities began. It was drawn by Dave Cockrum, who had pitched Legion characters to DC. He modified those designs for the X-Men and would base the Imperial Guard on the Legion. However, it was more than just the looks and powers that the X-Men would take from the Legion. Chris Claremont came aboard the X-Men and he knew what had to be done: focus on the characters.

There are lots of things you can point at as the reason for the X-Men's success, but one of the most important is how great the characters were. The X-Men felt like fully-realized characters compared to other Marvel books of the day. Go back and read those old X-Men comics and you'll be instantly drawn into the lives of the characters. Uncanny X-Men had amazing superhero stories, sure. Classics like the M'Kraan Crystal saga, "The Dark Phoenix Saga", "Days of Future Past", the Brood Saga, "Lifedeath", "The Trial of Magneto", and many more are all era-defining stories. However, what makes them so great is the quiet moments, the way they built their characters, how the events affected them.

Much like the Legion, a truly massive group of X-Men became the focus of the book during its most popular years. There was a web of relationships between all of the characters and little cliques within the greater group. If you don't know their histories, you can still enjoy them, but gain a greater appreciation once you know the past. One of the games that comic fans like to play is comparing who is who in the various universes. So, for example, saying the Avengers are the Marvel Justice League. The X-Men are Marvel's Legion, their success built in the same way.

The Legion cultivated a devoted fandom over the years thanks to the character. Fans learned to love them and wanted to spend more time in their lives. Others found them complex, but their fans gloried in taking ten minutes to describe the history of Starboy to a confused friend asking them for help. Their books were superhero soap operas and their approach was the one that Chris Claremont used to make the team popular again.

The X-Men became popular in the '70s and '80s not just because they were in cool fights with their enemies but because of who the team were. None of their stories would work so well if Claremont and company hadn't built up the characters and their lives, though. It's the exact same thing that years of Legion creators had done over the years, building the characters, making us love to spend time in their lives. The Legion made the superhero soap opera popular, but the X-Men perfected it.

Do you think that X-Men are Marvel's Legion of Superheroes? Do you think they copied the Legion approach or am I completely wrong? Sound off in the comment section below.

“It's no different than any other industry, if you're thinking about what amount of risk you are willing to take and then how are you going to feed that risk,” he added.

Boehly said Katz had impressed him from the start for his ability to identify and work with risk during his time with Guggenheim Partners.

“Daniel's real magic, when he worked on our trading floor from, let's call it like 2008 to 2012, he didn't take a lot of risks, but he said ‘no’ a lot,” he said.

The $160M disaster movie by Wolfgang Petersen went down in film financing folklore after it faltered at the box office and failed to gross enough to cover its P&A costs.

Boehly provided $19M in seed money for A24 as Katz launched the company in 2012 with David Fenkel and Joh Hodges. It was last publicly valued at $3.5 billion in June 2024.

“Everyone told me in Hollywood that there's no room for another distribution company,” recalled the businessman. “His early successes with Spring Breakers and The Bling Ring were really structured finance trades.”

“You're not really allowed to talk about that in the entertainment world because everything's creative and creator driven… what Daniel was really good at, because he sat on a trading desk and he understood risk and he understood math, he was really good at figuring out how am I going to get my money back using different windows.”

Starring James Franco, Selena Gomez, Vanessa Hudgens, Harmony Korine’s Spring Breakers premiered in competition in Venice and went on to gross $31M.

“Spring Breakers cost a couple million bucks to buy, and he ended up making 10 million bucks or so very quickly on, because he really understood that it's a structured finance straight," said Boehly.

He added that beyond Katz's business savviness, the company had also understood how to tap into social media to generate audience engagement as well as how to plug into trends of the moment.

“One of the things that A24 has done an amazing job at is being able to read the cultural zeitgeist. I think Civil War was really well timed; Marty Supreme was very well timed with Timothée Chalamet and his ascension as probably one of the top actors for the next couple of decades."

Boehly also highlighted A24’s strategy of growing a cohort of directors and actors, who returned to work with the company on a regular basis.

“He wants repeat customers. He wants the directors coming back… he wants the actors coming back… because then it's not a transaction, it becomes a recurring business with enterprise," said Boehly.

"So many people think about the film business, ‘Oh, it’s a transaction’. But if you're really thinking about how to build an enterprise, then you need to make sure that you have a recurring revenue base. And the way you do that in this industry is you get repeat users."

He also gave insight into how Katz constructs A24's slate in a way that enables it to work with established names and newcomers and turn a profit, suggesting that over a portfolio of 15 films, nine would be "the core bread and butter".

"It's a budget of 25 to 40 million bucks. “And then he'll take three big swings and make something that has the capacity to become multiple films out of the content… he'll take 1.2 times. So, he'll modify his expectations on the rate of return to achieve something that might have more enterprise value or longevity on the back of it.”

Celebrity chef Ina Garten will not be cooking up a freestyle for “ Dancing with the Stars ” in the near future.

Garten told Rose Byrne on a recent episode of her “Happy Hour” podcast that she would be too nervous to compete. She opened the floor by asking Byrne if she had ever “not done something because it was too scary,” before answering her own question.

“Somebody asked me to do ‘Dancing with the Stars,’” she said. “I thought, ‘Nobody needs to see that. articles.title: Guarding Stars Was Adorable, But Can We Talk About That Stalker Twist?
articles.summary: There was some soggy fruitcake amidst this Christmasy feast.
articles.content:
This year’s Christmas movie releases are in full swing now that it’s mid-November, and I knew I had to check out Guarding Stars with my Netflix subscription . I mean, it unites Gilmore Girls ’ Jared Padalecki with Gossip Girl ’s Leighton Meester , so I was in for the 2000s nostalgia alone. I was really digging this lighthearted rom-com (that’s sometimes an action movie), but then that twist just made me go “WTF!” Let’s talk about it. But be warned, there are SPOILERS ahead!

Before we get into my lows about Guarding Stars , I have to give the movie its flowers. I’ve seen a lot of holiday rom-coms, and this one had the right amount of sweetness and depth I want from this kind of movie. It follows the fake dating trope pretty much to a T, but I really enjoyed what Padalecki and Meester in particular brought to it as Jack and Hannah.

It’s the kind of movie where we all know they were going to fall in love by the end, but I was instantly curious about how these two were going to fall for each other. I like that they brought out the softness in each other despite both of them being otherwise hardened by their current lives, and I really liked the mother/son dynamic between Jack and Andie Macdowell’s Connie.

However, I thought the Guarding Stars really dropped the ball on the whole “stalker” plotline. Not that I’d expect it to be a huge part of the movie to begin with, but when it was revealed that Nadine was Jack’s stalker near the end, I was so taken aback. It felt way too convenient that one of two people he meets outside of his family and his bodyguard crew ended up being the stalker, and particularly having happened to be in the same place where he was hiding away.

articles.title: One Piece Is About to Unravel a Mystery That Has Kept Fans Guessing for 3 Years
articles.summary: Toei Animation One Piece's latest chapter has begun unraveling a mystery that the series introduced over three years ago, in May 2023, and it could change much of what fans know about the series. Given that One Piece is currently in its final saga, it was evident that the series would begin unveiling the mysteries it has […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One Piece 's latest chapter has begun unraveling a mystery that the series introduced over three years ago, in May 2023, and it could change much of what fans know about the series. Given that One Piece is currently in its final saga, it was evident that the series would begin unveiling the mysteries it has built up over more than 1,000 chapters. While several have been explained here and there, one of the most intriguing mysteries the series has kept concealed revolves around the Void Century. There are hundreds of speculations about what this century holds, but a few characters have been particularly connected to it.

Among the several characters tied to the Void Century , one of the most intriguing is Nefertari D. Lili, the queen of Alabasta during that era. She was one of the founding royals behind the World Government; however, she refused to become a Celestial Dragon and instead returned to her country. This has been unveiled and hinted at several times in the past, ever since King Cobra first mentioned the queen and revealed that she had also left behind a letter. The latest chapter hints that Robin may finally read this very letter, and it couldn't have been unveiled at a more perfect time.

One Piece Chapter 1195 had subtly revealed that a woman named Lili once lived in Elbaph, and now the latest chapter, 1199, unveils that what she left behind was a letter that Robin is about to read. It is now evident that this is indeed the same letter Cobra mentioned, potentially containing an important piece of information related to the Void Century. However, the timing of this revelation is also intriguing, as Luffy has mysteriously transformed into a rogue version of his Gear 5 appearance , displaying entirely monkey-like behavior and features. Perhaps the letter Robin is about to read could have something to do with this transformation.

It has been speculated that Lili was at the center of the conflict involving Imu and Joyboy, with some fans even suggesting a possible love triangle. That may very well be true, and Joyboy, as Nika, could also be connected to the form Luffy has now transformed into. One Piece still has a lot to explain about Luffy's new appearance, and with speculation already suggesting that this is a second version of the Sun God , feared as the destroyer of the world, the series has plenty of questions to answer. The Elbaph mural also hints at this very version. With the mention of Lili and a letter that is finally about to be read, the series has raised the stakes surrounding this mystery and the answers it is about to unveil.

The Void Century remains one of the most intriguing mysteries One Piece has concealed, and even a single piece of information about it could help connect the dots and reveal what actually happened during this period. By bringing Lili's letter into the picture alongside Luffy's mysterious new appearance, One Piece is in the perfect position to finally unveil some of its biggest secrets. Honestly, the series couldn't be better prepared to address these mysteries, and it should begin doing so in the next chapter without delaying any further.

articles.title: The Royal Family Barely Responded About Meghan Markle’s Dad. How Prince Harry Allegedly Feels

articles.content:

Since the onset of this legal matter and Thomas’ eventual arrest, the British Royal family has only lightly addressed it. Meanwhile, insiders are claiming Harry has strong thoughts on that.

Shortly after the news broke, Meghan Markle released a statement in which she said she was “deeply distressed” by the situation. The Duchess of Sussex also notably mentioned that in 2018, a letter was sent to the Metropolitan Police and Royalty and Specialist Protection, and it detailed allegations against Thomas. As Meghan explained, that letter was eventually shared with her and that she was later told that the situation was being investigated accordingly.

After the Thomas Markle claims publicly surfaced in October, the media attempted to receive clarification from Buckingham Palace on whether King Charles was aware of that letter. However, the British Royal Family reportedly opted not to comment on the matter, according to People . The news outlet reported that the palace felt that the situation was more so for the Sussexes to contend with.

Per reports, Meghan Markle has been “devastated” over this situation involving her father and has been trying to process it. As of this writing, Prince Harry has not explicitly discussed the case against his father-in-law. That hasn’t stopped insiders, however, from dropping claims about his feelings towards his relatives’ response or lack thereof.

These days, it’s rare that Prince Harry publicly discusses his family, from whom he remains mostly estranged. Despite where he stands with them, though, Harry purportedly takes issue with none of them coming to his and his wife’s aid at this time, per The National Examiner . A source for the outlet said:

articles.title: 'Madden' Sparks Backlash From Raiders Owner Mark Davis Over Father Al Davis' Portrayal: "That Hurts"

As John Madden 's life gets the biopic treatment, his longtime colleague and friend Al Davis ' family is not pleased with their late patriarch's portrayal.

Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis , whose father Al recruited Madden to coach for the NFL team when they were located in Oakland in 1967, criticized David O. Russell 's Madden for its "totally unfair" depiction his father (portrayed by Christian Bale ), who died at age 82 in 2011.

"It was full of turducken," he told USA Today of the movie, referencing the Thanksgiving dish Madden popularized.

Mark continued, "As far as representations of my dad, yeah, that hurts, and I did the best I could to protect him. It's absolutely a crime that they're able to treat people that have passed away and characterize them in ways that are unfair, and there's nobody around to protect their legacies. It's just unfair. articles.title: Noah Kahan Deserved a Lot More Grammy Love Than Just One Minor Nomination. Here's Why He Didn't Get It

articles.title: GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Are Exactly What Grand Theft Auto's Storytelling Has Been Missing
articles.summary: Courtesy of Rockstar Games For all the memorable characters Grand Theft Auto has introduced over the years, there's always been something a little off about how the series approaches its protagonists. They're often larger-than-life personalities with enough baggage to fill an entire criminal enterprise, yet their personal stories can feel surprisingly disconnected from the chaos happening around them. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google For all the memorable characters Grand Theft Auto has introduced over the years, there's always been something a little off about how the series approaches its protagonists. They're often larger-than-life personalities with enough baggage to fill an entire criminal enterprise, yet their personal stories can feel surprisingly disconnected from the chaos happening around them. GTA 5 made an ambitious attempt to address this by giving players three protagonists with wildly different personalities. It was an entertaining experiment, but it was a hard sell to get you to feel genuine compelled in their actual lives. This is especially apparent when you recall Rockstar didn't really bother expand upon their stories after the credits. That's where Grand Theft Auto 6 gets the narrative right.

Jason and Lucia are exactly the kind of protagonists I've wanted to see from this franchise. Rather than splitting attention between three people with competing ambitions, Rockstar builds its latest crime saga around a relationship that gives the entire adventure a much stronger emotional foundation. They're partners whose futures are tied together, for better or considerably worse, which means their actions take on an inherent emotional risk, adding an extra layer to literally everything they say and do. This shift makes an enormous difference, as it gives players a natural core to care about the about them, in one of the most dangerous professions: being a criminal.

One of the biggest strengths of GTA 5 is undoubtedly its three-protagonist setup. Michael, Franklin, and Trevor each bring something different to the table, and switching between them creates opportunities for comedy and conflict that wouldn't work nearly as well with a single lead. But that structure comes with a trade-off. The story constantly has to divide its attention between three separate lives, each with their own problems and motivations. Their paths intersect in entertaining ways, but the relationships between them rarely become the emotional foundation holding the entire experience together. They're memorable individuals first and a unified group second. I would not call that a flaw, as that's what GTA 5 set out to accomplish, but it does leave its narrative feeling less intimate than it could have been.

Jason and Lucia's relationship isn't some subplot that Rockstar occasionally revisits between heists. It's the connective tissue running through the entire experience. Their criminal ambitions are intertwined because neither character is simply pursuing some grand scheme in isolation. They're trying to build a future together, even when their circumstances make that prospect seem increasingly ridiculous. That gives their decisions a stronger weight. A dangerous job isn't just another opportunity to make money or create some spectacular mess. It's something that could affect the person standing beside them, that's a natural concept for any human to feel, whether its a spouse, a family member, or anything between. I find that considerably more compelling than simply having another protagonist to switch between.

Jason and Lucia don't need to constantly agree with each other to make their partnership interesting, nor does their connection depend on turning every interaction into some grand romantic declaration. Their chemistry comes through in the smaller moments, the banter, the disagreements, and the sense that these two people have developed a life together despite everything working against them. Rockstar has always been capable of writing memorable personalities, but giving those personalities a relationship worth investing in is a different challenge altogether. GTA 6 understands that distinction, and it makes Jason and Lucia considerably more interesting as a pair than either protagonist would be in isolation.

One of the things I find most interesting about Jason and Lucia is that their story doesn't have to stop whenever a mission ends. Rockstar has been building open worlds for years, where players can lose entire afternoons doing practically anything that catches their attention. Yet those diversions have often existed separately from the narratives unfolding in the main story. GTA 6 makes a more concerted effort to bring those two experiences together. Spending time with Jason and Lucia outside missions can reveal more about their personalities through conversations and interactions that respond to what's happening around them. Rather than relying entirely on cutscenes to develop its protagonists, Rockstar gives players opportunities to get to know them simply by spending time in their shoes.

This approach apparent in the smaller interactions between the two. Jason and Lucia can hold hands while exploring the world together, wait for one another when getting into a car, and even hold doors open for each other. None of these actions is particularly spectacular on its own, but that's precisely why I like them. They're the sorts of things that make a relationship feel… true, rather than something that only exists when the story needs an emotional moment. Rockstar's developers have discussed how these interactions evolved from individual mission ideas into features players could experience throughout the open world. It's a surprisingly thoughtful use of the freedom that makes GTA 6 so appealing in the first place.

I think this is an important step forward for the series because it makes the time between major story beats feel more meaningful. The best open-world games understand that their protagonists shouldn't disappear as characters whenever players decide to ignore the main objective for a while. I'd argue that's one of the greatest faults of the sub-genre, so its great to see GTA 6 take a stab at tackling this long-running problem. You aren't always watching Jason and Lucia's story happen. Instead, sometimes you're simply driving around together, and the game finds ways to make even that feel like part of it. It's ultimately a clever way to strengthen the central narrative and bring the open-world design closer together in unison. Personally, I hope Rockstar carries that philosophy into whatever comes next.

Do you think Jason and Lucia make for a more compelling protagonist duo than Michael, Franklin, and Trevor in GTA 5 ? Why or why not? Let us know below!

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has officially kicked off the Resurrection F arc with its newest episode, and with it has given Frieza's return a major upgrade compared to the original version. Dragon Ball Super has been offering up a newly enhanced take on the now classic TV anime series from over a decade ago, and the first episodes of the new series had revealed how the Battle of Gods arc had been upgraded from its original release . Now it's time to see how it works out in the next arc.

With the previous episode of Dragon Ball Super: Beerus wrapping up its take on the Battle of Gods arc as Goku and Beerus' fight had come to its end , the new remake series can now move forward with the next arc. Resurrection F had been one of the more divisive arcs from the original film and TV versions seen before, and this new remake offers a chance to make up from those previous missteps. And that seems to be heading in a promising direction already.

Following the post-credits scene at the end of the previous episode , the Resurrection F start has now begun as Dragon Ball Super: Beerus sees Sorbet and the rest of the surviving Frieza Force scouring the universe for the Dragon Balls. Coming to Earth, they are able to successfully wish to revive the villain thanks to Emperor Pilaf and his gang collecting the balls to make their own wish. And by the end of the episode, Frieza has come back to life. Which already makes it feel speedier than before.

The original version of the Resurrection F arc in Dragon Ball Super 's TV series only ran for 9 episodes compared to the 18 seen with the Battle of Gods arc, so it does raise some questions as to how long the arc is going to last for in the remake. With Battle of Gods wrapping up its own events within six episodes, the new version might end up moving through Frieza's return even quicker than that. But the overall episode count of the new series has yet to be confirmed as of this time .

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has been confirmed to share new versions of the Battle of Gods, Resurrection F and Universe 6 sagas before it comes to an end. It's likely going to continue through the rest of the Fall 2026 slate, and end sometime in January or February by the time it gets through all three arcs. With the three arcs spanning nearly 50 episodes during their initial run, and 19 episodes for the Universe 6 arcs, ending sometime during the Winter 2027 broadcast schedule does make a lot of sense .

There are still the Goku Black and Universe Survival Sagas left on the table for a potential remake of this kind, but nothing of the sort has been revealed to be in the works at this time. With Dragon Ball Super: The Galactic Patrol also now in the works as it plans to adapt one of the future arcs only seen in the manga , there could be a lot more Dragon Ball Super anime on the way than fans might realize.

What are you hoping to see in this new take on Frieza's return in Dragon Ball Super: Beerus ? How have you liked the reboot so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: 5 Common Misconceptions Even Longtime Fans Have About Batman, Especially When it Comes to Killing
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics Batman is one of the most popular characters to ever hit the comic book page, only rivaled by the likes of Spider-Man and Superman, and it seems that just about everyone knows about him to some extent. However, just because someone knows about something doesn't mean that they perfectly understand the character. Case in point, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Batman is one of the most popular characters to ever hit the comic book page, only rivaled by the likes of Spider-Man and Superman, and it seems that just about everyone knows about him to some extent. However, just because someone knows about something doesn't mean that they perfectly understand the character. Case in point, despite the incalculable number of people who connect to the Dark Knight, misunderstandings of his character only seem to grow more numerous over time. Today, we're dissecting five of the most rampant misunderstandings of Batman's character and going over what the truth about him is. Comic book characters may vary between runs, but that doesn't mean there isn't a specific standard they should be held to, and that's what we're looking at now.

Batman is a dark and brooding character. He slinks around in the shadows and has a scowl literally baked onto his cowl. He looks especially serious when compared with his most famous partners like the Robins and Superman, but he is far from a humorless character. When written well, Batman is actually really funny. He's not quipping like Spider-Man or anything like that, but he is a master of dry humor. Nobody expects Batman to be funny, even in DC itself, so every time he hits someone with what was clearly intended as a joke, it leaves them flabbergasted, which only makes it funnier.

Heck, even The Dark Knight Returns , the story foundational for the uber-serious, militaristic Batman persona that's so popular in the modern day, could be downright hilarious. In issue #3, he goes undercover to stake out Bruno's operations and chooses to dress like an old lady ranting about the price of alcohol. Batman can be a comedy genius when he wants to be, and a constant attempt to drain that from him makes his stories feel far more stilted and flat than they should be. A good joke can actually help build tension by giving them a break, prepping them for the storm about to hit, which is exactly where Batman's comedy is at its best.

This is one of the most common misconceptions about Batman that starts endless arguments, but I think that's mostly because people are arguing about different ideas. When people say that Bruce Wayne is Batman's mask, they point to endless examples of his playboy persona, or when he acts like a helpless and clueless stooge to keep his identity hidden. Without a doubt, this is a performance, a mask he wears, but so is Batman. When I argue that Bruce Wayne is the real man beneath the mask, I mean that Batman could not exist without Bruce. Batman is an idea born from Bruce's grief, an ideal that strives to use his pain to make the world a better place.

Bruce Wayne is Batman's heart. He's the man who funds the vast majority of Gotham's charities and social protection nets, who chooses to give criminals a second chance and help them find good jobs at Wayne Enterprises, who risks his life every night to keep what happened to him from happening to anyone else. Batman is the face Bruce wears when he fights criminals, and the playboy persona is the one he wears when he's fighting in social circles, but both are covers for the true man beneath, who you only really see when he's talking with someone he trusts, or in his own thoughts. Bruce Wayne is the man who fills out the mask, not the other way around.

Being Batman is obviously an extremely taxing and difficult endeavor. Bruce has had to give up countless opportunities at happiness to pursue his career as the Dark Knight, and when push comes to shove, he'll always put being Batman above just about everything else in his life. However, being Batman is not exclusively a burden. This idea that being Batman meant constant suffering and loneliness emerged from the Dark Age of comics and, predominantly, the Nolan trilogy. Seriously, Bruce gives up being Batman constantly in those movies. Regardless, if Bruce could give up being Batman in good conscience, he would, but he also enjoys being Batman.

It gives Bruce the chance to use the agony he's felt ever since his parents' deaths for something useful. Being Batman lets Bruce fight back against the unfailling tide of darkness that Gotham is always drowning in and pull others out of it. Just as much as being Batman is a sacrifice, it's also Bruce's path towards redemption. He chooses to be the Caped Crusader because it lets him help others in a way he couldn't in any other capacity, and Bruce is a man who wants to help everyone. Being Batman is also a positive, and while that doesn't outweigh the negatives it brings some days, there are days when it definitely does.

Again, all of these misconceptions are based in truth in some capacity, and this one is so easy to see. After all, Batman proudly proclaims that he's vengeance in the night, and his rage and despair at his parents' death definitely drive him to save the day. He's a man filled with rage that he's never let go of, but that's not the real reason he pushes himself to save the day. Batman exists to save people. First and foremost, the Dark Knight was created to keep what happened to Bruce from happening to anyone else. Batman doesn't defend Gotham because he wants to punch criminals, but because he wants to make it a better place to live.

Batman is definitely driven by his parents' deaths, but also by their lives. They were kind, hopeful people who gave everything they had to make their city a better place, and their generosity and nobility are what spur Bruce on more than anything. Batman is fighting so that nobody else has to, and his ultimate goal is to leave his city a better place than he found it. You wouldn't know it from a cursory glance, but Batman is driven by an unshakeable hope that things can get better and people can be saved. He helps because people need help, and that's even the main reason behind his refusal to kill.

Most of the time, Batman's refusal to kill is argued only to the point of his belief that it's wrong. However, far too few conversations about this dig into why that belief formed in the first place. It's this misunderstanding that his convictions only go that far, that killing is wrong because it is, that led to massive deviations from his character that have stuck in the public zeitgeist. The most popular examples, which have poisoned the well of this discussion seemingly beyond repair, both come from movie adaptations. Batman: Under the Red Hood and Batman Begins , respectively.

The "I won't kill you, but I don't have to save you" scene with Ra's al Ghul fundamentally misses the point of why Batman refuses to kill in the first place, and also completely messes up, given that Ra's was only unable to escape explicitly because of Batman's actions, which makes Batman a murderer. Any character who has to loophole their own morality clearly isn't interested in that morality in the first place, but I digress. The other big offender is Batman spewing the idea that if he kills once, killing again would become too easy, and that would make him less effective at saving people. That's far closer to what it really is, but the framing makes it sound like Batman is one murder away from becoming a serial killer, which you can check out for yourself right here. It's a scene that almost ruins this beautiful movie for me.

Play video The real reason Batman doesn't kill is that he values life. He fights so hard because he's personally felt the effects of losing someone he cares about, and has seen the terror death can cause. He's the son of a doctor and social worker, exposed to the cruelest reality a child could be at a young age, and he concluded that life is beyond precious. Batman truly, fundamentally believes that every life has value, to the point where even a monster like the Joker deserves to keep breathing because there is a chance, however impossible it seems, that he can change. Batman tries to save everyone . Especially his villains. He doesn't reject death; he treasures life, and that is an important and distinct difference. At the end of the day, Batman is driven by an endless belief that things can get better, and he's going to do everything he can to make that a reality for everyone.

Which common Batman misconception aggravates you the most? Or do you disagree with any of my points here? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A new Nintendo Switch 2 report has revealed four different open-world games coming to the console. None of the games are brand new, but rather ports. In this case, two are from the 2010s, while the other two are from the 2020s. And all four come from the same European publisher. Ubisoft. Unsurprisingly, three of these four games come from the series the publisher is primarily known for: Assassin's Creed . The fourth game, meanwhile, is a licensed release.

The new report comes from Nash Weedle , a well-known Nintendo insider with a decent track record of scoops. According to the insider, Ubisoft is preparing to bring the following four games to Nintendo Switch 2: Assassin's Creed Origins , Assassin's Creed Odyssey , Assassin's Creed Valhalla , and Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora . This would be pretty noteworthy because three of these games never came to Nintendo Switch. Only Assassin's Creed Odyssey did. So, this would be a potential introduction to three of these Ubisoft games for Nintendo purists. Unfortunately, this is the extent of the report, other than the note that the Assassin's Creed Valhalla port has been given priority among the four ports.

Assassin's Creed Valhalla is the 12th mainline installment in the long-running Ubisoft series that is sometimes a stealth series, other times an open-world RPG series. This installment is an example of the latter. It is also a successor specifically to 2018's Assassin's Creed Odyssey .

Upon release, the Ubisoft Montreal game earned a Metacritic range of 80 to 82 and would go to become one of Ubisoft's best-selling games of all time and the best-selling game in the series.

Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora is an action-adventure from developer Massive Entertainment, the studio best-known for The Division series. Upon release, it earned a 72 to 75 Metacritic range. This was obviously a disappointment and paired poorly with its commericial underperformance. That said, it is undeniably one of the best-looking open-world games of the generation .

Assassin's Creed Origins is another Assassin's Creed game from Ubisoft and the 10th major installment in the series, and a pioneering installment at that, as it was the first game in the series to be an open-world RPG rather than a stealth-action game. Upon release, it earned a Metacritic range of 81 to 85.

Lastly, there is Assassin's Creed Odyssey , the successor to Assassin's Creed Origins . It was released the following year in 2018 by developer Ubisoft Quebec. And while Assassin's Creed Valhalla is the commercial high point of the series, Assassin's Creed Odyssey was the best reviewed game in the series among the open-world RPGs. In the series as a whole, it falls below a few other earlier releases in the franchise. To this end, upon release, it earned a Metacritic range of 83 to 87.

Al of that said, and as always, remember to take this unofficial report with a grain of salt. So far, Ubisoft has not commented on it. We do not expect this to change for a variety of reasons, but if it does, we will update the story accordingly.

articles.title: The Hotel Bel-Air’s Menu Returns to Tradition
articles.summary: Everything old is new again, as classic hits are revived, from the Thai-style chicken salad to the house burger.
articles.content:
Since Wolfgang Puck's 2023 departure from the Hotel Bel-Air and its eponymous restaurant, the luxury lodging has been tweaking its Cal-Med menus with classical French techniques and hyper-seasonal ingredients. The approach was ambitious, evolving, at times even experimental . Yet the largely local dining clientele — 70 percent of weekly regulars are neighbors — who treat the place as a second home (or maybe a fourth, given their net worth) have made it clear they prefer familiarity over ingenuity. Under new executive chef Ralf Schlegel (far left), previously of The Peninsula in Beverly Hills, the kitchen has turned back toward the classics. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The bill of fare has long had a dedicated section of "Bel-Air Classics": the tortilla soup, the club sandwich, the chopped salad named for late No. 1 fan Nancy Reagan. Now, the restaurant has restored several other salads that had been relegated to off-menu, only-by-request status — Thai-style chicken, soy ginger BBQ salmon, burrata with squash — along with the house burger.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Has an Almost Impossible Task Ahead of It, And GTA Online Is the Reason
articles.summary: Courtesy of Rockstar Games Imagine spending more than a decade building your criminal empire, filling garages with cars you've painstakingly collected, buying properties across Los Santos, and turning a fresh character into an absurdly wealthy menace. Now imagine being told it's time to do it all over again. That's the awkward position Rockstar faces with Grand Theft Auto 6. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Imagine spending more than a decade building your criminal empire, filling garages with cars you've painstakingly collected, buying properties across Los Santos, and turning a fresh character into an absurdly wealthy menace. Now imagine being told it's time to do it all over again. That's the awkward position Rockstar faces with Grand Theft Auto 6 . Its predecessor isn't some aging multiplayer mode that players have been desperately waiting to abandon. GTA Online has grown into an entertainment platform of its own, with an enormous amount of content and a community that has spent years making Los Santos their second home. Following that is going to be a monumental challenge, regardless of how impressive Vice City turns out to be.

And honestly, I don't think simply giving players a new map is going to cut it. There's a reason people keep returning to GTA Online after all these years, and it isn't exclusively because they enjoy driving around Los Santos. They've built up characters with virtual lives that represent an incredible amount of time and money. Rockstar needs to give those players a compelling reason to start over without making them feel as though everything they've accumulated suddenly means nothing. Fortunately, there's a fairly straightforward way to approach this problem that SEGA has already experimented, with a positive result.

The challenge facing Rockstar isn't really about making a better version of GTA Online (though that's a given). It's the player base that leaving the original behind is worth it. That's a difficult proposition when you consider just how much the game has accumulated since its debut in 2013. Some players have been around practically from the beginning, and their characters have grown alongside the experience. They've purchased businesses and spent years acquiring things that newer players might not even realize exist. Even the most outrageous criminal empire represents a personal investment when you've spent that long building it. Starting over might be exciting for some, but I can absolutely understand why others would be reluctant.

Its unrealistic, though, for Rockstar to try to preserve everyone's entire criminal empire. The games are literally decade apart, and the tech involved is massively different. A new generation GTA Online also deserves a fresh economy, a new progression system, and its own reasons for players to chase that next big purchase. Carrying over billions in GTA$ or allowing veterans to immediately bring their entire arsenal into a new game would undermine much of that experience before it even gets going. But there's a meaningful difference between resetting someone's progress and wiping away everything they've collected. I'd happily start from the bottom again if it meant having a new world to explore and a fresh set of criminal opportunities to pursue. What I wouldn't appreciate is losing years of cosmetic purchases and collectibles simply because Rockstar wants everyone to begin with an empty wardrobe.

This might sound like an unusual comparison, but SEGA's Phantasy Star Online 2: New Genesis offers Rockstar a surprisingly good blueprint. The original Phantasy Star Online 2 had already been running for more than a decade when SEGA introduced New Genesis as a massive next-generation evolution of the experience. Players weren't simply moving into a new region with their existing progression intact. Character growth was reset, and much of the original game's equipment and progression systems didn't make the transition. However, SEGA made a particularly smart decision with one of the things players had spent years collecting: their fashion. A substantial range of avatar items and customization options carried over, allowing longtime players to bring their established appearance into the new experience. It wasn't a complete transfer of everything, but it meant that a decade of cosmetic collecting wasn't simply thrown away.

Rockstar should make players start from scratch in GTA 6 Online , but give them access to the clothing and cosmetic items they've purchased or earned throughout GTA Online 's lifespan. There might be some technical hurdles involved, especially if older assets need to be rebuilt to meet the new game's visual standards, but that doesn't make the idea any less worthwhile. In fact, Grinding Gear Games is already demonstrating another approach with Path of Exile 2 . The studio is bringing applicable cosmetic purchases from the original Path of Exile into its sequel, while gradually adapting its enormous backlog of microtransactions to work in the new game. Not every item is immediately available, but the commitment to preserving purchases is there.

I don't expect Rockstar to make everything from GTA Online compatible with a completely different game. Some things simply won't make sense in Vice City, and a fresh online experience needs room to establish its own identity. But cosmetics are a different matter. If someone has spent years collecting outfits and accessories, why should all of that disappear when they move to a new game? GTA Online has been an enormous part of the franchise's success, and the people who kept it alive deserve to feel that their time and purchases mattered. Rockstar doesn't need to let everyone bring their old empire into Vice City, it should consider letting players bring their visual selves along for the ride. GTA 6 Online has not yet been announced, but its evitable arrival is already setting the stage for conversations just like this.

How much of your GTA Online progress would you want to carry into the next game, and would you be willing to start your criminal empire all over again? Let us know in the comment section below.

Dancing with the Stars ' season finale is just around the corner on the 2026 TV schedule , and there's a lot to talk about. articles.title: After 114 Years, the Beverly Hills Hotel Gets a (Night)life
articles.summary: The landmark’s biggest expansion yet adds a supper club, a cocktail bar and, at long last… a screening room.

Wearing a hard hat and a tailored suit, Beverly Hills Hotel general manager John Scanlon surveys the most significant expansion in the iconic Pink Palace's 114-year history. Amid the BRRRAAAP ! of drills and SKREEEE ! of scraping metal, he outlines a slate of new amenities, a decade in the making, including a supper club, a screening room and a cocktail bar.

"I'm going to bed at night dreaming about this and waking up thinking about it," says Scanlon, a Dorchester Collection veteran who previously ran London's 45 Park Lane. "It's the first thought that comes into my head in the morning: 'Where are we at? What have we got to do today?' Right now, in the lead-up to their simultaneous debut in the coming weeks, the answer is: a lot. Finalize the menus. Hire more staff. Approve the live acts. Close out permits. Eyeball every aesthetic detail. On a terrace, among the property's paddle-shaped banana leaf plants, Scanlon says in his Irish brogue, with traces of exhilaration and exhaustion, "I'm obsessed."

Later, over a lunch of McCarthy salads at the Polo Lounge, alongside the hotel's new food-and-beverage head Megan Doherty, Scanlon explains that this is all an attempt to better serve guests, especially locals. A consultant — in his accounting, a "social anthropologist" — asked regulars what they wanted as the hotel considered renovations to a sizable swath of neglected, interconnected square footage, on the lobby level to the left of the red carpeted entrance, ranging from an unpopular bedroom suite to a '90s-era business center that "nobody was using anymore." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Foremost, it turned out, was a desire for a real nightlife option for party-hardly Beverly Hills. The solution is The Supper Club: a 94-seat, high-glam ovular room with skyline views of Century City that aims for neo-retro, akin to Delilah in West Hollywood. Open until 1 a.m., it will feature a no-photos policy, throwback palm tree motifs, coastal Italian dishes from chef Mattia Agazzi (previously of Gucci Osteria) and a sequence of live evening performances, including five-piece bands, which are curated by music director Alex Le Roux, an in-demand industry booker for events like the wedding of Brooklyn Beckham and Nicola Peltz. "This concept perfectly fits into the heritage of this hotel, but allows us to do something fresh," says Doherty, who previously ran operations for star L.A. chef Evan Funke.

The research also produced a 14-seat screening room, which is tricked out for sound to handle record-release listening events. Its design by Ken Fulk (clients include Pharrell Williams and Gigi Hadid) is inspired by the Holmby Hills screening room of , Louis B. Mayer's daughter and Hollywood's preeminent hostess, where she showed films to friends before release.

For his part, Scanlon seems perhaps most enthused about a new, yet-unnamed cocktail bar — "very intimate, very elegant" — which he promises will rival the Dorchester's offerings, as well as a lobby-oriented lounge, boasting a wraparound veranda, which will present afternoon tea service: "We'll have bespoke teas and hand-painted china from Royal Crown Derby and custom sterling silver tea stands that have been made by Arthur Price. A key challenge for the new spaces is competing with the landmark existing ones, chiefly the Polo Lounge, the Fountain Coffee Room and the Cabana Café. "Our guests know and love and really connect with them, and there's this nostalgia there," Scanlon explains. "They are tractor beams. So, with what we're doing now, it's been about, 'What can we do that's distinctive?' They need to shine on their own." He adds, looking up from his McCarthy salad, "a lot of places take the most popular dish off the menu. That's crazy to me. Make another popular dish!"

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Jujutsu Kaisen has been gearing up to make a reveal about the anime's future during Jump Festa 2027 later this December, and the franchise has given Yuji Itadori and the others a cool makeover before this coming update. Jujutsu Kaisen kicked off the first phase of the Culling Game arc from Gege Akutami's original manga series earlier this year, and thankfully confirmed that a fourth season was already in the works. And we're going to get a new update on it soon enough.

Jujutsu Kaisen Season 4: The Culling Game Part 2 has been announced to be in the works , but not much has been revealed about when it's potentially going to hit. That's likely to change with a new update coming our way as part of Jump Festa 2027 later this December as Jujutsu Kaisen is one of the major Shonen Jump franchises showing something off. And to get ready for it, MAPPA has dropped a cool makeover for Yuji and the others with a special new visual. Check it out in action below.

Jump Festa 2027 is this year's iteration of Shueisha's annual event where they showcase some of their biggest manga and anime titles. Taking place over the December 19-20 weekend in Japan , this is where fans get the first major updates for all of the new projects now in the works for the coming year and beyond. Jujutsu Kaisen has yet to reveal what exactly it's going to showcase during its own panel for the event, but it's still exciting nonetheless as we'll get an update on the franchise's future.

Jujutsu Kaisen Season 4: The Culling Game Part 2 has yet to confirm a concrete release date, window or international release plans as of this time. All that has been revealed thus far is that it will be continuing through the Culling Game arc, and that Takeru Sato would be taking over as director from Shota Goshozono for studio MAPPA. The rest of the production staff, potential returning voice cast, new additions and more have yet to be revealed. So any update on those fronts would absolutely be welcome.

The Culling Game Arc is the penultimate arc of Gege Akutami's original Jujutsu Kaisen manga, and that means this next season is going to bring the anime one crucial step closer to the grand finale. The fallout of Kenjaku's plan for the tournament combined with Sukuna's mysterious plans for Megumi and Yuji will combine together to expand into even more chaos in the coming episodes. It's all going to get much worse for Yuji and the others, undoubtedly.

It's been about five or so months since Jujutsu Kaisen Season 4 dropped its last major teaser, so Jump Festa 2027 would make for a perfect time for the franchise to drop a new trailer heading into the new year. It would also be great to get a release update for the episodes, but for now catch up with it all now streaming with platforms such as Crunchyroll, Hulu, and Netflix in the meantime. Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The live-action Mash Burndead gets his best look yet in a new official update. 2027 is going to be a huge year for Mashle: Magic and Muscles fans with the anime's return and the live-action movie. Based on Hajime Komoto’s Weekly Shonen Jump hit, the anime still has a lot of chapters left to cover even though the manga reached its conclusion in 2020. Season 2 concluded in March 2024 , and a third season was announced soon afterward, the wait was still longer than expected. The anime is all set for its return in January next year as part of the Winter 2027 lineup.

On the other hand, the franchise is also expanding next year with a live-action movie. The live-action announcement earlier this month caused quite a lot of buzz, especially since fans weren't expecting a new adaptation around the same time as the anime's return. While the series has yet to share more updates on the live-action movie, the official X handle drops a new look at Mackenyu, who will be playing the role of Mash Burndead. Mackenyu is known for his excellent performance in several live-action adaptations, including One Piece , where he is loved by fans for playing the role of Roronoa Zoro. The visual reveals his appearance as Mash while he eats a cream puff, something the character probably loves more than anything else.

The movie will hit the Japanese theatres on March 19th, 2027. However, international fans still await a release date, which might take at least a few months. Live-action movies aren't always released in U.S. theatres, but there's still a possibility that fans will be able to watch the movie with subtitles on a streaming platform. However, nothing can be certain before the movie's premiere. While Warner Bros. and Fuji TV are overseeing the film, CREDEUS is handling the production, and TOHO is overseeing the distribution across Japan. The movie has yet to release a full-length trailer, but fans already have high expectations after watching the teaser thanks to the casting and the visuals.

The third season will continue the Divine Visionary Selection Exam Arc, the third story arc of the manga. Depending on the episode count, we can also expect the upcoming season to adapt some chapters from the fourth Tri-Magic-Athalon Divine Visionary Final Exam Arc, the second final story arc. The second season finale confirms that the secret about Mash having no magic power is revealed to the kingdom.

It's no surprise that the public is extremely outraged, and they want nothing more than to see him get executed, just like every other non-magic user in the kingdom. However, Mash's friends and Wahlberg manage to buy him some time. His fate will be decided after the candidate exam is over. The third season also needs to focus more on his origins that will explain the reason he is unable to use magic at all.

articles.title: Adam Driver Finally Reveals the Strangely Hypocritical Reason Disney Passed on Hunt for Ben Solo Movie
articles.summary: Another day, another ridiculous reason why Disney decided to pass on The Hunt for Ben Solo—the movie that might have eased some of the ill will left behind by the line "Somehow Palpatine has returned." Now, Adam Driver is telling fans what they've pretty much known the entire time: the official reasoning behind Disney's decision […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Another day, another ridiculous reason why Disney decided to pass on The Hunt for Ben Solo —the movie that might have eased some of the ill will left behind by the line "Somehow Palpatine has returned." Now, Adam Driver is telling fans what they've pretty much known the entire time : the official reasoning behind Disney's decision to not move forward with The Hunt for Ben Solo . That reason? Well, Ben is dead, of course— a quandary that Star Wars has successfully tackled multiple times (Darth Maul, anyone? Palpatine, anyone?).

Driver recently sat down with Sam Fragoso on the Talk Easy podcast, where the two discussed everything from his enlistment in the Marine Corps to his time at Juilliard. Of course, the conversation turned to Star Wars, as it usually does, and Driver was frank about why the finished script (penned by Steven Soderbergh) was shelved. “The reason I was told, I’m not going to guess someone’s intention, the reason we got was Ben Solo was dead," the actor said. The reasoning is flimsy at best, considering that Lucasfilm had thrown its support behind the movie, as well as the fact that Star Wars has never been a story to shy away from the potential to come back from the dead, or a character's redemption after death. And that's not even counting the numerous petitions, billboards, and protests that arose after fans heard the news .

For one of its animated fares, that might have been the case. But death has never been a hard-and-fast rule in a galaxy far, far away. It's been a roadblock, sure, but never a definitive ending for a character. With Force Ghosts and the World Between Worlds right there, there were plenty of ways to find Ben Solo—which had obviously been put to use, as Soderbergh's script was finished by the time it was pitched. It's also not the first time that Disney has shied away from an IP that centered itself around a villain of sorts. They also canned The Acolyte , a more adult series whose main character used the dark side of the Force , and one that some fans felt was "the first and only real fresh direction for a franchise that is stale and can't seem to move forward."

Overall, it's disappointing that Disney refused to give the film a chance, especially since it was helmed by the iconic Soderbergh, who had an incredible team behind him to bring the script to life—including Driver, who worked with him throughout to bring Ben Solo back. What's even more disappointing is that Disney now seems intent on relying solely on nostalgia farming to ensure that another reception like the one that the franchise received for The Rise of Skywalker doesn't happen again, clinging to the beleaguered "Space Dad" trope with Star Wars: Starfighter , as well as the poorly received Mandalorian & Grogu . But it seems that, despite what Dave Filoni hinted at , The Hunt for Ben Solo is officially dead.

articles.title: Anthony Mackie Ranked His MCU Screen Partners (And Shots Fired At Sebastian Stan)
articles.summary: The dude didn't even hesitate.
articles.content:
Anthony Mackie knows how to keep a Marvel press tour interesting, especially when Sebastian Stan 's name comes up. The two actors have spent years giving each other grief in interviews, and I have to imagine that, by now, Stan knows better than to expect a compliment when someone hands Mackie a microphone. Still, this bit of friendly trash talk is pretty ruthless. With another Avengers movie closing out the 2026 movie schedule , the former Falcon-turned-Cap has popped up again in a clip ranking his MCU screen partners, and shots have been fired at Stan.

The three names on the list were Chris Evans , Ramirez, and Stan. Essentially, that's a fairly brutal choice for Mackie, considering how long he's worked with Evans and Stan in the MCU, while Ramirez was sitting right there, ready to hear where his new Captain America thought he ranked.

That's one way to rank acting ability. Mackie had good reason to bring up the hardware. Stan won a Golden Globe for his performance in A Different Man in January 2025, and he also earned a Best Actor Oscar nomination for playing Donald Trump in The Apprentice . Both films marked pretty significant moments for an actor many Marvel fans still know primarily as Bucky Barnes. And Mackie was clearly keeping track.

Anyone who's followed these two beyond the release of new Marvel movies knows this is pretty standard behavior. Mackie and Stan first appeared together in 2014's Captain America: The Winter Soldier and, later, their verbal squabbles in 2016's Civil War made a real splash with audiences. Watching Sam and Bucky bicker was also half the fun of their eventual Marvel series , 2021's The Falcon and the Winter Soldier . Their Mackie and Stan's interviews together were sometimes even better.

articles.title: The More I Read The Dungeon Crawler Series, The More Worried I Get About The Peacock Series
articles.summary: I can't be the only person wondering this between chapters.
articles.content:
I dove into Dungeon Crawler Carl back in July , and now that I'm almost caught up on the book series, I have some major thoughts about the upcoming streaming series on Peacock . Mainly, I'm worried about how the streamer intends to pull this off, and whether I'll actually get to see the series the way we all want to.

Dungeon Crawler Carl is one of the best-selling book series of recent years, and its name recognition is growing. That said, it's not Harry Potter , and while the upcoming series for that HBO Max show received a massive budget for its streaming debut, I'm not sure DCC would get the same.

Not only is the budget for Dungeon Crawler Carl massive, but each floor of the Dungeon also transforms the series entirely. A lot of sets will need to be scrapped entirely and rebuilt, which will only impact the amount of time it takes between seasons. The events of the book only take place over the course of a few months, but I imagine adapting it all to streaming would take years, if not longer.

If there's one thing I hate in this modern era of television, it's waiting multiple years for new seasons. As mentioned, however, I'm not sure how it could happen any other way. This is going to be a big series, and if it isn't, it's going to disappoint a lot of people.

It's also going to feature many returning voice stars for the new episodes too.

Blue Eye Samurai Season 2 has confirmed the returns of stars such as Maya Erskine as Mizu, Brenda Song as Akemi, Darren Barnet as Taigen, Masi Oka as Ringo, and Kenneth Branagh as Abijah Fowler. There might be other potential returning faces from the first season that have yet to be revealed at this time, but new additions to the cast for the coming season include Jonathan Pryce as Old Violet, Joel Kim Booster as Priest Ando, and Sherry Cola as Kuma. But there's still much we don't know about the coming season yet.

Blue Eye Samurai Season 2 will be picking up right from where the first season left off as Mizu has entered a very tenuous agreement with Fowler . "For the first time, she’ll have to confront what it’s like to stand out as Asian in a sea of white faces," the creators have previously teased. Blue Eye Samurai is returning for its second season next year, but has also confirmed it's now in the works on its third but final season coming after that. No release window has been set for the final season as of this time, but at least fans can rest easy knowing that they will be able to see Mizu's story come to its end. Whatever kind of ending that might be for her. What are you hoping to see in Blue Eye Samurai Season 2? Let us know your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: 3 Horror TV Shows Far More Disturbing Than They Needed to Be, Including A Beloved Cult Classic Series
articles.summary: Horror is one of the most consistently well-represented genres on the big screen, but its chances to shine on television are often far less frequent. While the idea of horror movies is one that audiences around the world are incredibly familiar with, horror TV shows are nowhere near as prevalent. However, there are a few […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Horror is one of the most consistently well-represented genres on the big screen, but its chances to shine on television are often far less frequent. While the idea of horror movies is one that audiences around the world are incredibly familiar with, horror TV shows are nowhere near as prevalent. However, there are a few essential horror shows for fans of the genre, each proving that horror can be just as effective on the small screen as it can anywhere else. The episodic nature of storytelling might make sustaining horror stories a little more difficult, but when done correctly, the results can be truly exceptional.

Over the years, there have been a few genuinely terrifying horror TV shows that have kept viewers up at night. However, some horror shows actually take their scares to a whole new level, delivering stories and imagery far more disturbing than was strictly necessary. In doing so, these shows managed to secure themselves a lasting place in the nightmares of many among their audience, giving us truly horrifying developments that we likely won't ever forget.

AMC's The Terror is an anthology series that many horror fans hail as one of the genre's finest new additions. Its first season was based on Dan Simmons' novel of the same name, which in turn was a fictionalized account of the real lost expedition of Captain Sir John Franklin to the Arctic in the mid-19th century. Subsequent seasons explored different stories, but the one narrative idea that connected them all is the show's dedication to delivering particularly terrifying and unsettling stories.

Not only is The Terror an incredible horror TV show , but it seems to fundamentally understand not just how to scare its audience, but how to make them feel genuinely uncomfortable. By establishing a bleak atmosphere and using practical effects to detail the horrific fates of its characters, The Terror provides a viewing experience that can only be described as addictively unpleasant. In taking dark subject matter and uncompromisingly exploring its most horrific implications, The Terror manages to be even more disturbing than most could ever have suspected it would be.

Hannibal took the characters and ideas of Thomas Harris' famous novels and turned them into something that felt completely original. Primarily focusing on the relationship between FBI profiler Will Graham and the brilliant psychiatrist and cannibalistic serial killer Hannibal Lecter, Hannibal 's general premise seems to suggest it might be a distinctly dark spin on the traditional police procedural genre. However, the reality is that it's actually a far more surreal and unsettling exploration of its titular character, as well as the wider implications of his actions on the world around him.

Celebrated as a horror TV show truly ahead of its time , Hannibal 's knack for delivering disturbing imagery in increasingly inventive ways somehow felt both unexpected and organic. Fans of previous adaptations involving the character typically find the show to be particularly disarming in its stark depictions of violent crimes and the stomach-churning nature of some of its scenes. Even in its most horrifying moments, though, Hannibal finds a way to make its scenes feel bizarrely elegant, which only serves to heighten just how surprisingly disturbing the show can be.

Channel Zero might not be a name that carries much weight outside of dedicated horror circles, but to those who saw the show, it's likely to immediately conjure up some truly nightmarish images. Perhaps the most deeply unsettling show of its era, Channel Zero's basic premise doesn't necessarily indicate anything overly groundbreaking. Inspired by internet creepypastas — amateur horror stories shared via message boards and forums typically depicted as true events — Channel Zero is another horror anthology series that proved way more disturbing than anyone expected.

Embracing the nature of the creepypasta source material, Channel Zero opted not to specifically explain every plot point, but rather to allow its grotesque imagery and ideas to speak for themselves. This made it an incredibly underrated horror series , largely because it so perfectly captured the essence of the mindless but effective horror stories it sought to adapt. Based on its premise alone, you might not expect Channel Zero to be overly frightening, but its use of unique and unforgettable monsters and truly nightmarish images made it something that very few viewers will ever be able to forget.

articles.title: Rian Johnson Cites Curry Barker as Reason to Be Optimistic About Future of Indie Filmmaking: ‘Youtube Is Just What Sundance Was in the '80s’
articles.summary: Rian Johnson is hopeful about the future of indie filmmaking. articles.content:
Rian Johnson is hopeful about the future of indie filmmaking.

During a converation at Marrakech Film Festival on Sunday afternoon, the "Star Wars: Last Jedi" and "Knives Out" director specifically cited Youtube as one of the most effective ways for early-career filmmakers to get their movies discovered.

Johnson reflected on a recent conversation he had with 27 year-old director Curry Barker who was discovered on Youtube before catapulting to fame with his box-office breakout "Obsession." "YouTube to me isn't a new form or some new scary paradigm," Johnson said. "YouTube is just what Sundance was in the '80s. It's a way to get your movie out there so that people can see it." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Abdul El-Sayed Mocks Trump and Ted Cruz's Cruel Rhetoric on 'The View,' Jokes He Wants 'Jihadist Leprechaun' Printed on a Hat

Johnson acknowledged that traditional film festivals still play an important role in launching indie filmmakers' careers, but argued that online platforms have opened up opportunities that didn't exist for previous generations.

"Even though there are a lot of things that are really hard right now about starting out as a filmmaker, that's one of the exciting things," he continued. "Besides festivals, there are also other ways to build audiences, by making shorts and getting them out there and people discovering them. And there's a million different ways to get your feature out there."

Barker's career is a particularly compelling case study. The filmmaker first built an online following alongside comedy partner Cooper Tomlinson through their YouTube channel "that's a bad idea," before pivoting into horror with the 2023 short "The Chair," which amassed millions of views. His next project, the found-footage horror film "Milk & Serial," was made for just $800 and released for free on YouTube in 2024, where it became a viral sensation. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The film's success attracted Hollywood's attention, leading Barker to sign with UTA in 2025 and eventually make the leap to theatrical filmmaking with "Obsession." The supernatural horror film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in 2025, where it sparked a bidding war before landing distribution with Focus Features. Released theatrically in May 2026, the microbudget production became a breakout box-office success.

Filmmakers including Kane Parsons, whose viral "Backrooms" videos led to an A24 feature, have similarly turned Youtube followings into Hollywood opportunities.

Johnson, meanwhile, has firsthand experience with the traditional festival pipeline. His 2005 feature debut, "Brick," starring Joseph Gordon-Levitt, premiered at Sundance, where it won a special jury prize.

"There’s something really special about watching someone’s first feature," Johnson said, praising Marrakech's commitment to showcasing debut and sophomore features. "You know they have been cooking it and its been building in their mind and they’ve been thinking about it, so in some ways there’s nothing more expressive or purer than seeing a first feature from someone."

He reflected on how challenging it was to find a wide audience for "Brick," which he began writing when he was 22. "I spent my 20s trying to get it made and failing and I finally made it when I turned 30," he said. "So it took me eight years to get it made. And all this time the idea was baking and stewing in my head."

Their shoestring budget only allowed them 19 days to shoot the entirety of the film but said "I think anyone who’s making a movie on that tight a schedule knows the only way to do it is by prepping and knowing what you’re doing when you get in there."

"And you just do it because you have to do it," he continued. "I don’t know if the less resources felt like less resources, it just felt like this is the way we’re making this particular movie."

Still, Johnson argued that the platform itself matters less than the work filmmakers are putting into the world.

"If you make something that connects with people, and if you have something to say and you have something in your heart, and you've practiced your craft so you can do it effectively, that's still an incredibly rare thing and something that everybody is looking for," he said. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Whether it gets into a festival or whether people start discovering you online or whatever, there's so many things that make it hard," Johnson continued. "But I truly believe that is the gold coin that everybody is searching for in the world. So the more opportunities you have in the world to do that and get your work out there, the better, I think."
