Saturday morning cartoons library is finally set to make its streaming debut after 23 long years, and it's going to be available totally for free. Tubi has been making great strides in the past year especially to make Warner Bros. Animation classic library more accessible than it ever has been before , and that's even more true thanks to the fact that all of these shows have been available for free on a rotational schedule that's seen lots of shuffled releases.

Tubi this Fall had kicked off a slate of releases for Kids WB! block fans that saw shows like Mucha Lucha and more return to streaming after being missing in action for basically decades outside of their initial home video releases or digital storefront purchases. But as November comes to an end and December 1st fast approaches, Tubi has revealed a new slate of streaming releases coming to the platform that notably includes the fan favorite, Xiaolin Showdown .

As Tubi announced on their official social media, Foster's Home for Imaginary Friends, Mucha Lucha , and Beetlejuice will be leaving the platform on December 1st. But in their place will be new additions to the platform Xiaolin Showdown, Wacky Races, MAD, and Duck Dodgers . It's also been revealed that a number of classic Cartoon Network movies and specials will be returning to the platform at the same time including Dexter's Laboratory: Ego Trip, Ed, Edd n Eddy's Jingle Jingle Jangle, Ed, Edd n Eddy's Hanky Panky Hullabaloo, Ed, Edd n Eddy's Big Picture Show , and Ed, Edd n Eddy's Boo Haw Haw.

The full breakdown of new additions to Tubi on December 1st is as such:

Kids WB! might not be as fondly remembered as other competing Saturday morning cartoon blocks at the time such as Fox Kids and One Saturday Mornings, but it had a lot of gems under its belt for action fans. Originally created by Christy Hui in 2003, the series introduced fans to a group of kids training in specialty martial arts fighting to protect mysterious artifacts known as the Shen Gong Wu. Episodes often had contests for these items with one Xiaolin warrior facing off an enemy, and often saw the items bounce back and forth between the sides.

The series had lots of fun action and often had an imaginative third act which saw multiple different types of contests take place that pit different skills against one another for these magical items. It led to episodes that really took fans by surprise, and three seasons that told a serialized story (before coming back for a reboot years later). Now that it's coming to Tubi, it's the perfect time to go back and see why it was so fun on Saturdays.

2027 will open with an exciting Winter lineup where fans will be getting the sequel seasons of Mashle: Magic and Muscles , Shangri-La Frontier, and more. The anime will begin its Japanese broadcast on January 6th, 2027. The anime is based on an underrated web manga written by Monsho Sasakibara and illustrated by kanco. The manga barely has fans in the West, but the anime announcement is creating quite a lot of buzz thanks to the trailer. The story centers around an ordinary Japanese man who died in a traffic accident at the age of 30.

In his final moments, he swore to himself that if he got another chance, he would live a long life and leave behind proof of his existence. As if his final wish was granted, he reincarnates as an elf in a fantasy world with a lifespan of 1000 years. The story follows his journey as he strives to become a living legend in order to wash off the regret of not doing anything great in his previous life.

articles.title: Fans Wanted One Thing From The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, But the Movie Fumbled It
articles.summary: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters at last, bringing to the big screen the story of Haymitch’s games, the Second Quarter Quell. It’s a story that fans of Suzanne Collins’ The Hunger Games series have been eager to see since the book was released in 2025 and finally helped readers understand […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters at last , bringing to the big screen the story of Haymitch’s games, the Second Quarter Quell. It’s a story that fans of Suzanne Collins’ The Hunger Games series have been eager to see since the book was released in 2025 and finally helped readers understand where the true origins of what would ultimately be Katniss’ rebellion began but there was something else very specific fans were looking for with the film. Fans wanted to see the original cast of The Hunger Games film — Woody Harrelson, Jennifer Lawrence, and Josh Hutcherson — reunite as their characters. It was truly the one things that fans really wanted.

And The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping technically provided, but what should have been a triumphant moment capping of Haymitch’s story and providing a beautiful bit of closure on the saga as well as a lovely moment for fans, the scene just didn’t live up to expectations. A genuinely meaningful moment was sacrificed in the name of fan service and it’s disappointing.

In the movie, after a montage of Haymitch’s post-victory life, walking us through him being the “worst victor ever” as he promised Maysilee he would be and saw him bury Tribute after Tribute, we eventually get to the now-older Haymitch on his birthday. This time, though, there will be no reaping. The square has vines growing over the old platform and Haymitch is joined by Katniss and Peeta. It’s a very short moment with some throwaway dialogue. The trio talk about the place being peaceful, about it being a nice place to mark his birthday, a suggestion about going out to the lake that Haymitch declines to instead go to the meadow. As he goes to leave, Katniss and Peeta thank Haymitch and he smiles before going to the meadow to watch the geese.

While the scene sounds nice, it doesn’t really have that much emotional resonance to the story and it also feels wildly out of place. First, the whole scene is styled oddly. The wigs on the cast — particularly on Josh Hutcherson’s Peeta — are distractingly bad. There’s also how they character are portrayed. The scene simultaneously feels like it is happening the first reaping day after the war which we know is not true but also like it is a good bit into the future. Haymitch also comes across as too much at peace and too easily “healed”. Instead of feeling like a somber moment to sit with the journey and understand just how much has truly changed, the scene feels more like a “here is what you asked for” in the most superficial way possible. It just doesn’t work.

The book scene would have actually been a better epilogue and still would have allowed for fans to have that much desired on-screen reunion. In the book, the scene is where it is revealed that Haymitch has been telling his story to Katniss, finally opening up about his Games and everything he lost. We also see Haymitch given goose eggs and Peeta builds an incubator for him as a way to honor Lenore Dove. The framing gives space for Haymitch to finally, perhaps for the first time in decades, to sit with his grief and process everything he’s lost. It’s a moment of healing and hard-won peace that has a lot of weight. It isn’t a “happily ever after” like the movie scene frames things, but there is a hopefulness in it that is raw and beautiful.

The emotional resonance of how Collins framed things in the book would have been not only a great way to cap off the film (and would have made up for some of the things that didn’t make it to the screen ) but also would have let fans truly see Harrelson, Lawrence, and Hutcherson as the iconic characters in their true forms one more time. With Sunrise on the Reaping likely the final chapter of the story, this emotionally weighty moment is what the ending deserved. And it’s what we should have gotten.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters now.

“There’s a new trailer dropping on Monday… am I allowed to have said that?” Atwell, who returns to the franchise as Peggy Carter, told fans on Friday night.

Disney has also announced a sneak peek for November 30 during The Wonderful World of Disney: Holiday Spectacular on ABC, but this is believed to be a different tease. A few hours prior to Atwell’s omission, some 7,000 miles away in Qatar, co-director Joe Russo had also hinted at fresh drops before the picture’s opening by Disney on December 18, telling fans to keep checking their feeds. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

Talking in a fireside chat at the Qatar Film Committee ’s second Doha Industry Days, Russo explained that the four teasers, preceding an official trailer this summer, had played an integral role in the final version of the film.

He said it had been a way to connect with the fans, which was essential because the audience landscape had changed so much since Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame in 2018 and 2019 respectively.

“I have to work extra hard to subvert your expectations and be aware of who you are as a viewer and how you’re changing,” said Russo.

“The last time I did this, in 2018, 2019, is very different than now because we've been through a pandemic; lots of people spent a lot of time on social media. Movies saw a tremendous downturn, streaming saw a tremendous upturn, and now that all seems to be reversing. So, it shifts constantly,” he said. “You have to be a futurist to try to predict where the market is going.”

“I have to interact with the fans in order to understand what is moving them, what is working for them,” he said. "What we've been doing with Doomsday is very different than the last time we did this because the speed of conversation on the internet is even faster than it was in 2018, 2019." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“I had this idea, why don't we start the story a year early? Why don't we start dropping clues in the year leading up to the movie… we did four trailers that were sprinkled out,” he continued.

Kicking off on December 23, 2025, the first trailer showing Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) returning home, unpacking his Captain America suit, and holding a baby. A teaser on November 30 showed Thor (Chris Hemsworth) praying to Odin for strength. This was followed onJanuary 6 2026 drop featuring the X-Men and a January 13 teaser, featuring the Wakandans and Fantastic Four.

“We've done a series of tags around the characters because the story actually started in January of last year, and you've been watching it slowly unfold and these are all pieces of something that are going to equal two and a half hours of your time on December 18,” he said.

“It's slowly investing them [fans] emotionally. But I'm also getting feedback as that's happening and we can make adjustments as we go, based on what people are tracking or not tracking,” he continued.

“It’s a very complicated story also, so I have to make sure that they're following each little crumb we give them. If they get the wrong thing from it, then I have to make adjustments, knowing that they might have the wrong idea about it.”

Talking about his return to the Avengers franchise alongside brother Anthony Russo, Joe Russo said he had been reluctant at first because of the immense challenge of pulling off a Marvel movie at that scale.

He credited Robert Downey Jr., who played Tony Stark/Iron Man in Avengers: Endgame , with planting the seed for a return to the franchise, with his revelation that he was down to play Victor von Doom/Doctor Doom.

“He's a very dear friend of mine, but I also think he's the greatest actor of his generation. This is a supremely talented, charismatic human being. And he translates incredibly well on a global scale. There's something about the nature of his performance that translates,” said Russo.

“There's a style that belongs to these films that allows them to work in every market around the world. He just embodies that,” he said.

Russo said Robert had gently enquired whether he was up for coming back to the Avengers franchise over dinner a couple of years ago.

“I was still recovering from Infinity Wars and Endgame . And I was hesitant… he's smart, he doesn't push too much, he just kind of dropped the idea on the table and let it sit there, and then after dinner, he brought it up again, and I was like, ‘I don't think I could do it, I'm still too tired.’ And then this festered for a little bit. And he didn't even really tell me what he was going to do going back,” recall Russo.

“And then another conversation happened where he said, ‘You know, I'm going to play Doom'. And I said, ‘That's a really clever idea”. I can see a corollary there. There are thematics, greatest hero, greatest villain. There's a multiverse. There's a reason for being. There's a compelling idea there. And I went, ‘Well, of course, who else could play the greatest villain other than you.”

“It started to simmer in my brain a little bit. But we didn't have a story. You can't just show up with an empty canvas, so I still said no."

Russo credited longtime collaborator, screenwriter Steve McFeely, with coming up with the premise that gave a way in to writing Doomsday , after they had been pitching ideas back and forth. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

“Steve McFeely called me and said, ‘I have a crazy idea about how this works… what would happen if you left the cameras rolling at the end of Endgame ? What’s the very next scene that happens,” recounted Russo.

“I said, “That's really risky for a movie that had the level of success it did. You’re going to impact people's emotional investment in it… this could blow up in your face,’ and then I went, ‘I love it’,” he continued.

“The concept was like that's a very happy ending for one character. And what if happiness is finite, and what if you have to take happiness from someone else to create your own happiness… What happens in that story? That’s where I went, ‘Right, I know what to do with this.” The idea that like there was a cost to a happy ending."

articles.title: The Hunger Games Prequel Just Put Up A Huge Number At The Box Office
articles.summary: The Hunger Games is back in a big way.
articles.content:
We all knew The Hunger Games : Sunrise On The Reaping was going to open to a big number this weekend, but exactly what big meant was unclear. Experts seemed cautiously optimistic it would be over one hundred million dollars at the domestic box office, but it turns out that caution wasn’t needed. Hunger Games not only made $100M, it blew past $100M.

You can check out the full top ten from the weekend, as per The Numbers . Those figures notably include a decent opening for I Play Rocky considering its budget and a fine enough hold for Johnny Depp ’s Ebenezer , which reminded everyone he’s still a bankable star last weekend…

I’ll get to the other movies in a bit, but before that, we need to talk about Sunrise On The Reaping a little bit more. The four initial Hunger Games movies, which were released between 2012 and 2015 all grossed between $650M and $900M at the worldwide box office. They were also collectively a major pop culture force that came up regularly in casual conversation. Unfortunately, 2023’s Ballad Of Songbirds & Snakes , which follows the story of President Snow prior to gaining power, didn’t have the same appeal and grossed less than $350M worldwide.

articles.title: Is GTA 6 Being Purposely Review Bombed? New Player Poll Has a Very Clear Answer
articles.summary: Rockstar Grand Theft Auto 6 has had an insane start, but after 8 years of full-scale development and 13 years since GTA 5, it's finally here. Now, with everything from game content leaks to accusations that its Game Awards entry was bought, to a slew of weird reviews (both positive and negative), every detail about the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Grand Theft Auto 6 has had an insane start, but after 8 years of full-scale development and 13 years since GTA 5 , it's finally here . Now, with everything from game content leaks to accusations that its Game Awards entry was bought, to a slew of weird reviews (both positive and negative), every detail about the first week of this game's run has come under scrutiny. But now it looks like some of those reviews might be part of a review-bombing campaign meant to tear the game down for not being a copy-and-paste of its predecessors.

What GTA 6 's actual reception by critics and audiences is is something that we might never know . But between its likely impossible 99% on Metacritic and the obvious review bombing from a certain subset of the fandom, the waters get much murkier. So ComicBook decided to do a poll to get to the bottom of things, and while we obviously pulled from a smaller sample size, the answer is clear: this game, while far from perfect, is definitely being review-bombed on the player side, and while it currently sits at 5.6, its rating should actually be closer to an 8 out of 10 (and we did the math to prove it).

How would you rate GTA 6 so far?

While a large number of people who voted haven't actually played yet, the highest data point is from those who would rate the game between 8 and 10 out of 10. And the first few comments on the poll, including gems like "How presumptuous of you to expect that I feel any obligation to waste my money time and space on that overrated overhyped and overpriced dating sim," pretty much prove the reasons behind the review bombing: GTA 6 , while flawed in terms of gameplay by things like poor frame rates and glitches, such as with weapons and vehicles, is also a game that puts a relationship featuring two imperfect people at its center, and there is a focus on that dynamic that wasn't present in other games—something certain players can't abide.

If you want the math based on the same standards Metacritic uses to get their overall rating, here you go: 8–10 (midpoint 9): 44 ÷ 56 = 78.6%. 5–7 (midpoint 6): 7 ÷ 56 = 12.5%. 0–4 (midpoint 2): 5 ÷ 56 = 8.9%. Score = (0.786 × 9) + (0.125 × 6) + (0.089 × 2) ≈ 8.0.

We might never actually know what the unbiased rating for a game like GTA 6 would be, especially considering the chaos that surrounded its rollout, the anger toward how Sony handled its release, as well as their removal of physical media and multiplayer potentially costing even more in the future. The game's narrative takes a strong social stance, as all other GTA games have, but with the relationship central to the storyline, it's proven to be too big a turnoff for certain gamers who participated solely in previous games' more edgelord aspects.

articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Kadokawa A classic action series has surprisingly announced it's coming back with a new anime revival to help celebrate its 15th anniversary. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A classic action series has surprisingly announced it's coming back with a new anime revival to help celebrate its 15th anniversary. If you are of a certain age, you might have noticed how there have been many classic anime and manga franchises coming back with new anime adaptations . Revivals and reboots have led to a lot of nostalgic successes in the last few years, and that's opened the doors to all sorts of new releases for fans to keep an eye out for. That's the case for Aria the Scarlet Ammo too.

The anime adaptation for Chugaku Akamatsu and Kobuichi's Aria the Scarlet Ammo light novel series is now celebrating the 15th anniversary of its original anime debut , and Kadokawa has confirmed that the franchise is going all out for the occasion. Aria the Scarlet Ammo is returning with a new anime short scheduled to make its debut next year, and has revealed the first look at some of the new and returning faces fans will see in action with the revival.

Officially titled Aria the Scarlet Ammo Corto , the new revival anime short is currently scheduled for a release next year. No concrete release date or potential international release plans have been announced as of this time, but it's going to feature familiar faces behind the scenes. Original series writer Chugaku Akamatsu is overseeing the script together with the Kenji Saito with Yoshifumi Sasahara is directing the new revival at BELLNOX FILMS. It's not a familiar production staff from the original series, but it will sound familiar.

Returning voice cast members announced to return for Aria the Scarlet Ammo Corto include the likes of Rie Kugimiya as Aria H. Kanzaki, Junji Majima as Kinji Toyama, Mikako Takahashi as Shirayuki Hotogi, Mariya Ise as Riko Mine, Kaori Ishihara as Reki, and Ayako Kawasumi as Jeanne d'Arc. New additions to the cast making their debut in this new revival short include Emiri Iwai as Lisa Ave du Ank, Miyari Nemoto as Minuet Holmes, and Anzu Haruno as Nemo Rinkarun. They can be seen in action with this first look poster you find above.

Aria the Scarlet Ammo likely isn't the first action series you think of when imagining all of the potential revivals and reboots that could be coming down the pipeline next, but it's likely one of those 2010s anime gems that just shook loose in your memory. The series is set in a school where students are trained in a deadly martial art known as Butei that teaches them how to use various weapons and other assassin skills. When Toyama is attacked by an assassin setting out to kill Butei fighters, he's soon saved by the prodigy Aria.

Aria the Scarlet Ammo technically ran for two seasons, but the second season was more of a spinoff story about a different character connected to Aria. So this is the first proper continuation of the anime since that first season came to an end in 2011. It's a return from the 2010s wave of franchises , and we're likely to get much more. How do you feel about Aria the Scarlet Ammo making its comeback? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: 5 Marvel Teams That Deserve a Comeback More Than Ever
articles.summary: Marvel Comics was the bestselling purveyor of superheroes for ages, but that has changed in the mid '20s. DC is on top and the House of Ideas is floundering. However, one place where they've managed to keep fans reading is their team books. Marvel is putting out some fantastic team books right now, with Fantastic […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Marvel Comics was the bestselling purveyor of superheroes for ages, but that has changed in the mid '20s. DC is on top and the House of Ideas is floundering. However, one place where they've managed to keep fans reading is their team books. Marvel is putting out some fantastic team books right now, with Fantastic Four, X-Men, Uncanny X-Men , and Avengers all impressing various parts of the fandom. The House of Ideas has always had some excellent teams; as great as the Justice League or Justice Society or Legion of Superheroes are, Marvel's teams are often just a little better. The publisher has decades of excellent team comics under their belt.

One could make the argument that the A-list teams are doing well because they are the A-list teams, but it's much simpler than that – they put the best creators on those books. Marvel is full of great teams that they aren't really doing anything with despite having the creators to make them work. The publisher needs a shot in the arm and these teams could give it to them. These five Marvel teams deserve a comeback, giving the House of Ideas more weapons in the sales war.

Guardians of the Galaxy was MCU perfection and it made the team a household name. However, it wasn't using the original version of the Guardians of the Galaxy, it was using the rebooted one that had been introduced 8 years before in Annihilation . This became the version of the team that Marvel Comics started using and there's an entire generation of Marvel fans who have no idea that they aren't the originals. The first version of the team isn't from the present, but the 31st (well, originally 30th) century.

In this future, the Earth was invaded by the Badoon, resulting in humanity being enslaved by the alien conquerors. The Guardians of the Galaxy –Vance Asto, Martinex, Charlie-13, and Yondu – fought to save humanity, with members like Starhawk, Nikki, Aleta, and Stakar joining up. They'd sometimes come back to the present, hanging out with the Avengers and other groups of heroes. The team has been all but forgotten, but honestly, give Al Ewing a chance to do this team, set in the future, and you'll get something brilliant. The original Guardians are amazing and they deserve another chance in the sun.

I'm an older fan. Back in the day, the library down the road from my house had Marvel books. They were mostly New Universe comics, so well-printed toilet paper for the most part, but they also had two books that would go down as some of my favorites – X-Factor (Vol. 1) and New Warriors (Vol. 1). The '90s were the thirtieth anniversary of the Silver Age Marvel Universe and the publisher was going out of their way to highlight this and create a new breed of heroes. The New Warriors were meant to be the modern equivalent of those classic teams, an all-new group of heroes that would form the next generation of the Marvel Universe.

Night Thrasher, Speedball, Nova, Namorita, Marvel Boy/Justice, and Firestar made a splash right away, thanks to the brilliant creative team of Fabian Nicieza and Mark Bagley. However, despite that strong start, they would never reach their promised position as the next generation of heroes and since then no one has even tried to make it happen. The New Warriors is an excellent group, full of cool heroes, and they are exactly what Marvel needs. The last time Marvel talked about bringing them back, they were able to anger both sides of the political divide, so this time, they should play them straight – what happens when the next big thing fails? The New Warriors have so much potential and it's about time they reached it (I can work up a pitch in about a day, Marvel).

The Avengers are Marvel's greatest team , leading the publisher to create new versions of the group. The first time was the premiere of the West Coast Avengers, giving the western half of the United States their own superheroes. Eventually, someone at the company decided to take this idea – a group of heroes protecting a particular geographic area – and play it for laughs. Thus, the Great Lakes Avengers were born. The team was meant to protect the Great Lakes region, a major commerce corridor for both the United States and Canada, but the members of the team were basically the not-quite ready for primetime players.

The group consisted of Mr. Immortal, Big Bertha, Doorman, Dinah Soar, and Flatman, each of them with powers that could be cool, but were just ridiculous enough. They were the joke team and their return in the mid '00s GLA: Misassembled (a title meant to lampoon both JLA and "Avengers Disassembled") helped make Dan Slott into a hot creator and was the first major return of Squirrel Girl. The Great Lakes Avengers are a team that is perfect for this age of Internet humor and Marvel should be trying to figure out a way to make them work (sadly, I don't have a pitch for this one).

Marvel has two Canada adjacent superteams, which isn't that weird, but still strange that it has two of them it does nothing with, especially with the amount of Canadian creators they have under contract. Alpha Flight was created by Chris Claremont and John Byrne, serving as an important part of Wolverine's history. They were the superhero arm of Department H, the secret Canadian organization that was charged with protecting the Great White North from superhuman threats. The first volume of Alpha Flight ran for 11 years and a 130 issues, becoming a rather beloved part of the Marvel Universe.

The team of Canadian heroes – Guardian, Vindicator, Sasquatch, Shaman, Box, Snowbird, Northstar, Aurora, and Marrina – have gone through numerous permutations over the years, with its latest role being an international superteam based in space, defending the Earth. However, Marvel needs to just go back to basics, bring back the Canadian government team, and let them have adventures. There's so much that can be done with them and it's about time they got another chance to shine.

The X-Men first debuted as a teen team, but they didn't really catch on. The second, older version of the team did, but eventually, Marvel wanted to try a teen mutant team again. This led to New Mutants , a book that became a beloved part of X-history and introduced the next generation of mutants. It would turn into X-Force , which was the young adult team, leaving the House of Ideas in need of a new group of teen mutants for the '90s. This led to the creation of Generation X , the group headlined by Jubilee, Emma Frost, and Banshee.

The team consisted of mutants with bizarre powers like Chamber, Husk, Skin, Penance, Mondo, and M, something of a commentary on teen culture of the team (if you were there, you'd understand; the '90s were when alternative culture became mainstream). The book's quirky art style from Chris Bachalo and Mark Buckingham turned heads and it became a rather beloved, if a tad bit niche, mutant book. They faded away in the early '00s before a reboot in 2017 that was great, but I'm pretty sure I was the only reading. The X-Men are doing good, but if Marvel could nail a new Generation X, things would be even better.

What Marvel teams do you think deserve a major comeback? Do you think they could help Marvel turn the tides? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.content:
"Sunrise on the Reaping" caught fire at the domestic box office, collecting a sensational $120 million in its opening weekend while reinvigorating Lionsgate's "Hunger Games" franchise.

The dystopian prequel is one of just five movies this year to launch above $100 million, joining the company of "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" ($360 million), “Toy Story 5” ($159 million), “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie” ($131 million) and “The Odyssey” ($123 million). All of those films eventually surpassed the $1 billion mark globally. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Cannes Condemns Five-Year Prison Sentence Against Iranian Palme d’Or Winner Jafar Panahi and Pleads for International Support

“‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ posting an impressive $100 million-plus debut reinforces just how vital 'The Hunger Games' remains as a movie franchise,” says Paul Dergarabedian, Rentrak’s head of marketplace trends.

"Sunrise on the Reaping" coincided with another big release — albeit not at the movies. Rockstar’s video game “Grand Theft Auto VI" launched after years of anticipation, earning a staggering $3.79 billion on its first day . It's expected to set a sales record for entertainment across any medium.

“Many have speculated as to whether the release of ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ would hurt ‘The Hunger Game’ at the box office, and I think the marketplace has already spoken," adds Dergarabedian. “There’s plenty of time to play ‘GTA VI’ and make it to a theater to see ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ this weekend."

On top of pitched competition at home, initial ticket sales for "Sunrise on the Reaping" are notable because they're not far off from original saga. For reference, 2012’s “The Hunger Games” ignited to $152 million, followed by 2013’s “Catching Fire” ($158 million), 2014’s “Mockingjay Part 1” ($121 million) and 2015’s “Mockingjay Part 2” ($102 million). Nearly a decade after those movies, starring Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson, concluded their run, the studio revived the young-adult property with 2023's "The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes," an origin story about Panem's cruel leader, President Coriolanus Snow. Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One Piece 's live-action series is fast approaching its return to Netflix next year, and it's one step closer to that launch with the start of a new wave of behind-the-scenes videos showing off more of the series' production. One Piece has been an incredible success for Netflix ever since the live-action series first made its debut . Quickly renewed for not just one, but two new seasons, the team behind it all has been hard at work on adapting Eiichiro Oda's massive manga series for the past few years.

One Piece: The Battle of Alabasta is the third major season of the live-action series as it sees Luffy and the Straw Hats heading into Alabasta in order to save Princess Vivi's kingdom , but it has yet to confirm a proper release date as of this time. But now that seems closer than ever before as One Piece will begin to release a series of special behind the scenes videos to give fans a better look at how Season 2 all came together. It's time to get hyped.

One Piece: The Battle of Alabasta is currently scheduled for a release with Netflix sometime in 2027 , but has yet to nail down a more concrete release date or window as of this time. This new wave of behind the scenes videos for the second season kick off a new project that will likely lead to the reveal of when this third season is finally coming our way. With promotional materials for the franchise heating up once more, it's time to start looking ahead to what could be coming our way in this new season.

One Piece: The Battle of Alabasta will be expanding its roles for some of the major players who debuted in the second season such as Mikaela Hoover as Tony Tony Chopper, Charithra Chandran as Princess Vivi, Sendhil Ramamurthy as Nefartari Cobra, Lera Abova as Nico Robin, and Joe Manganiello as Sir Crocodile ( who has been steadily teasing his return for the past few months as well ). Serving as the Straw Hats' first major battle on the Grand Line, this could be a major turning point for the franchise.

One Piece: The Battle of Alabasta will also be introducing many new faces to the expanding cast with the introduction of this new region too such as Xolo Maridueña as Ace , Cole Escola as Bon Clay, Awdo Awdo as Mr. 1, Daisy Head as Miss Doublefinger, Emilio Sakraya as Koza, Omid Abtahi as Toto, Jamie Ward as Pell, and Nabeel Khan as Chaka revealed thus far. But there will likely be many other new faces revealed the closer we get to Season 3's big debut in the coming months.

With the franchise revealing more behind the scenes information for the second season, it's going to give fans the best look yet at how production has been thinking in their approach to it all. This is going to be very important heading into the third season as the future of the live-action series remains uncertain , but we'll have to see how it shakes out soon enough. But what do you want to see from One Piece 's live-action series next? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A remaster of an entire and iconic PS1 trilogy of games is now available for $2.54. This is less than $1 per game and is unsurprisingly the cheapest the remastered trilogy has ever been available. While the games in question are PlayStation games from yesteryear, this new deal does not come via the PlayStation Store, but via Fanatical, which has Steam codes available at this price until December 1.

More precisely, until December 1, Fanatical is giving out Steam codes for Tomb Raider I-III Remastered available for $2.54. This is a 2024 collection that features remasters of 1996's Tomb Raider , 1997's Tomb Raider II , and 1998's Tomb Raider III , all from Core Design, the original developer behind the series before Crystal Dynamics took over. Whether these are the best Tomb Raider trilogy in the series is debatable, but it is certainly the most iconic, and an absolute steal at $2.54. That said, PC users may already own these games because they were given away for free on Epic Games Store earlier this year .

As you may know, the second and third of these Tomb Raider games are notably PS1 console exclusives. The first game, though, was actually a Sega Saturn exclusive at launch, before coming to other platforms, including the PS1.

Good, But Not Great Remasters Upon release in 2024, Tomb Raider I-III Remastered from Aspyr earned a 71 to 75 Metacritic range, which isn't great, but it's not bad either. It's decent. That said, its user review score on Steam is actually a bit higher than this, with 83% of Steam user reviews rating the game positively.

Positives of the remastered collection are how faithful they are, and that they include the expansions rather than lock them behind a separate purchase. The graphics are also appreciably improved. Unfortunately, the controls of the games weren't appreciably improved, and the bad news is the controls of the PS1 originals don't hold up well. The camera also isn't very good, and there is a lack of modern quality-of-life features, such as autosaves. To this end, the remaster makes revisiting the PS1 games much easier in 2026; however, they don't modernize the games enough for first-time visitors. In other words, while nostalgia is not required, it is recommened.

Those who end up checking out these nostalgic action-adventure games from yesteryear should expect to fork over at least 40 hours to see the trilogy through from start to finish. Completionists, meanwhile, will need roughly 90 hours with the Lara Croft games.

If this PS1 deal does not tickle your fancy, there is another great PS1 deal right now, and this one is available via the PlayStation Store, where a PS1 classic from 1997 has been discounted to $2.39 .
